---
title: "Stage 2: Stints, Segments, and Identification"
output: html_document
---

Results come from the pipeline (`targets::tar_make()` in the project root);
this report only reads and displays them. A stint is a stretch of play with the
same players on the pitch; a segment is a stint split further at goals and
15-minute clock edges. The identification diagnostics use the shot-volume
model; volume, xG, and big chances share the same design, so collinearity is
identical across them.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Run from the project root whether knit by tar_make() or by the Knit button
root <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("_targets.R")) "." else "..")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
```

```{r read}
stints <- tar_read(stints)
stint_table <- tar_read(stint_table)
segment_table <- tar_read(segment_table)
player_mins <- tar_read(player_mins)
overlap <- tar_read(overlap)
```

## 1. Stints

Building the stint and segment tables checks that every open-play shot is
counted once and that both reproduce the stage 1 team-match table exactly.

```{r stints}
show_table(stint_overview(stints, stint_table))
show_table(stint_table |>
  group_by(league) |>
  summarise(stint_rows = n(),
            median_minutes = round(median(minutes), 1),
            shots_per_90 = round(90 * sum(n_shots) / sum(minutes), 2),
            xg_per_90 = round(90 * sum(xg) / sum(minutes), 3),
            big_chances_per_90 = round(90 * sum(big_chances) / sum(minutes), 3),
            .groups = "drop"))
```

## 2. Segments

```{r segments}
cat(sprintf("Segments: %d\n", nrow(tar_read(segments))))
show_table(segment_table |>
  group_by(time_bin) |>
  summarise(segment_rows = n(), minutes = round(sum(minutes)),
            shots_per_90 = round(90 * sum(n_shots) / sum(minutes), 2), .groups = "drop"))
```

## 3. How minutes are distributed

```{r minutes}
show_table(minutes_table(player_mins))
```

Goalkeepers get defensive effects but no offensive ones.

```{r goalkeepers}
show_table(goalkeeper_table(stint_table, player_mins))
```

## 4. Teammate overlap

Outfield players with at least `r IDENT_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD` minutes. Overlap is
the share of the lower-minute player's time spent on the pitch with the other.

```{r overlap, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_overlap(overlap)
show_table(overlap_summary(overlap))
show_table(top_overlap_pairs(overlap, player_mins))
```

## 5. Design conditioning and precision

Standard errors a Poisson shot-volume model could achieve without shrinkage, as
a percentage change in shots per 90, against the spread of team attack effects.

```{r precision}
show_table(precision_table(tar_read(precision)))
```

## 6. Shrinkage and threshold choice

Effective df is the number of player parameters the data can support at each
prior SD; where the posterior SD is close to the prior SD, the data adds little.

```{r ridge}
show_table(tar_read(ridge))
show_table(tar_read(thresholds))
```
